Free subscribers will need to become paid subscribers to receive full story summaries. #TXLEGE Dennis Farris guest column : "Lives Are on The Line as Texas Lawmakers Debate Drone Ban, " via The Hayride** \-- "I've lost too many friends in the line of duty. When lives are on the line, we must do everything in our power to ensure first responders have the best possible tools to protect themselves and the public. That's why I must weigh in to oppose Texas lawmakers push to pass House Bill 41 - a well-intentioned but misguided piece of legislation that would force law enforcement and firefighters to abandon one of our most effective tools for saving lives: drones. Drones have revolutionized emergency response. They can be deployed instantly, providing officers with real-time intelligence before they step into dangerous situations. In active shooter incidents, fires, search-and-rescue missions, and disaster recovery efforts, drones allow first responders to quickly and accurately assess threats, locate victims, and make high stakes decisions - without putting human lives at unnecessary risk. I've seen it firsthand. When someone is lost in the wilderness or trapped under rubble, thermal imaging on drones has helped locate them when every second counts. When armed suspects flee into the night, drones offer aerial thermal imaging that keeps officers and civilians safe. Drones navigate environments that human responders can't: collapsed buildings, chemical spills, raging floodwaters, and dangerous terrain. Yet, instead of recognizing their life-saving value, HB41 would force police and fire departments to throw out these critical tools because they contain foreign-made parts. Why? There is concern foreign-made drones pose a security threat, but right now there is no specific evidence backing this fear. In fact, Congress already mandated a federal security study on these drones, set to be completed by December 2025. Texas legislators are rushing to ban them before the facts are even in. Legislators shouldn't pass a ban with very real life-and-death consequences based on theoretical threats. Law enforcement has been outspoken against this bill, and their main concern is the rapid timeline the bill imposes for stopping use and procurement of this technology. Departments would have no time to transition their drone programs and no good options for replacing their current drones. Right now, American manufacturers simply do not produce enough drones to replace the foreign-made models at the scale first responders require. Those that are available cost much more and often lack the capabilities law enforcement relies on - meaning agencies will either be forced to cut their drone programs entirely or spend astronomical sums on inferior equipment. It would be like telling people to throw out their iPhone and replace it with a $3,000 flip phone because the chip in their smartphone isn't American-made. This issue shouldn't be about politics or splashy anti-China headlines. Officer safety is on the line. Texas has always stood by its first responders, ensuring we have the support needed to protect our communities. Restricting access to drones will make our work more dangerous, put officers and firefighters at unnecessary risk, and ultimately jeopardize the very communities we are sworn to protect. We owe it to every first responder who has put their life on the line to ensure they have the tools they need to come home safely. HB41 is a step in the wrong direction. Let's not let fear dictate policy when lives--both first responders' and civilians'--are at stake. Dennis Farris is President of the Austin Retired Police Officers Association and has had a 30-year law enforcement career." #TXLEGE "After the failed attempt to impeach AG Paxton, state senators wants to change Texas' impeachment law " ($) "Batteries hold promise of clean, reliable Texas energy, if problems can be overcome " ($) STATE GOVERNMENT " Ag Commissioner Miller Makes Splash at EarthX with Water Warnings" TEXANS IN DC John Cornyn guest column: "I've worked hand-in-glove with President Trump to accomplish his agenda during his first 100 days" ($) 2025 " Business, community leaders rally behind $987M Alamo Colleges bond" BUSINESS NEWS " American Airlines loses $473M as demand falters, momentum 'quickly shifted' on tariffs" ($) " Southwest Airlines posts $149M loss, cuts guidance on 'macroeconomic uncertainty'" ($) NEWS FROM AROUND THE STATE FW REPORT: "Fort Worth Opera returns to Bass Performance Hall with first full-scale production in 6 years " THE TEXAN: "House Partially Passes $3 Billion Dementia Prevention Research Institute of Texas Legislation " AAS: "Gov. * **TOP NEWS**

"**Four Texas school districts at risk for state takeover after 2023 ratings released,** " Texas Tribune's **Sneha Dey** \-- "At least four Texas school districts could be forced to shut down their chronically underperforming schools or submit to a takeover from the state, based on annual state ratings released Thursday morning.

The Texas Education Agency released its A-F grades for the 2022-23 school year, the first complete set in five years. Ratings had not been released due to court battles and pauses to the rating system during the COVID-19 pandemic.

The Beaumont, Midland, Fort Worth and Wichita Falls school districts all have one or more campuses that failed state ratings for at least four years in a row, putting them at risk of bruising state penalties.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/77a80487-5d30-4c08-b1e4-3fc9f7b5a549?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Of the 8,539 public schools evaluated in the state, 19.3% got an A. Another 33.6% got a B and 24.7% got a C. About one in five campuses failed to meet academic standards, with 14.8% earning a D and 7.6% earning an F.

Performance scores for schools and districts are determined based on three categories: how students perform on state tests and meet college and career readiness benchmarks; how students improve over time; and how well schools are educating their most disadvantaged students.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/77a80487-5d30-4c08-b1e4-3fc9f7b5a549?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Overall grades declined for many campuses since the 2021-2022 school year. Half of the state's campuses received A or B grades, a decline of about 20 percentage points from the previous school year. The state only released partial scores that year.

TEA Commissioner **Mike Morath** attributed that decline to a drop in academic growth as schools worked to recover from the pandemic.

Many school district leaders, meanwhile, have attributed the declines to stricter college and career readiness standards. For the first time, schools had to show that 88% of their graduating high school students were college or career-ready to get an A, up from the 60% benchmark in previous years. About 10,000 more students met the requirements to prove college and career readiness.

"We keep raising the bar so that Texas is a leader in preparing students for postsecondary success," Morath said at a press roundtable.

The release of the A-F ratings comes after [legal battles](https://substack.com/redirect/e2d7ebac-ad36-416d-87d8-48211ef45613?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over changes to how schools are scored. More than 120 school districts sought to block the release of the 2023 ratings because they said TEA had not given them adequate notice before rolling out stricter college and career readiness benchmarks.

Earlier this month, an appeals court cleared TEA to make the 2023 A-F grades public, ruling that Morath did not overstep his authority when he changed the scoring metrics." * **#TXLEGE**

**Dennis Farris guest column** : "**Lives Are on The Line as Texas Lawmakers Debate Drone Ban,** " via The Hayride**** \-- "I've lost too many friends in the line of duty. When lives are on the line, we must do everything in our power to ensure first responders have the best possible tools to protect themselves and the public. That's why I must weigh in to oppose Texas lawmakers push to pass House Bill 41 - a well-intentioned but misguided piece of legislation that would force law enforcement and firefighters to abandon one of our most effective tools for saving lives: drones.

Drones have revolutionized emergency response. They can be deployed instantly, providing officers with real-time intelligence before they step into dangerous situations. In active shooter incidents, fires, search-and-rescue missions, and disaster recovery efforts, drones allow first responders to quickly and accurately assess threats, locate victims, and make high stakes decisions - without putting human lives at unnecessary risk.

I've seen it firsthand. When someone is lost in the wilderness or trapped under rubble, thermal imaging on drones has helped locate them when every second counts. When armed suspects flee into the night, drones offer aerial thermal imaging that keeps officers and civilians safe. Drones navigate environments that human responders can't: collapsed buildings, chemical spills, raging floodwaters, and dangerous terrain.

Yet, instead of recognizing their life-saving value, HB41 would force police and fire departments to throw out these critical tools because they contain foreign-made parts. Why? There is concern foreign-made drones pose a security threat, but right now there is no specific evidence backing this fear. In fact, Congress already mandated a federal security study on these drones, set to be completed by December 2025. Texas legislators are rushing to ban them before the facts are even in. Legislators shouldn't pass a ban with very real life-and-death consequences based on theoretical threats.

Law enforcement has been outspoken against this bill, and their main concern is the rapid timeline the bill imposes for stopping use and procurement of this technology. Departments would have no time to transition their drone programs and no good options for replacing their current drones. Right now, American manufacturers simply do not produce enough drones to replace the foreign-made models at the scale first responders require. Those that are available cost much more and often lack the capabilities law enforcement relies on - meaning agencies will either be forced to cut their drone programs entirely or spend astronomical sums on inferior equipment. It would be like telling people to throw out their iPhone and replace it with a $3,000 flip phone because the chip in their smartphone isn't American-made.

This issue shouldn't be about politics or splashy anti-China headlines. Officer safety is on the line. Texas has always stood by its first responders, ensuring we have the support needed to protect our communities. Restricting access to drones will make our work more dangerous, put officers and firefighters at unnecessary risk, and ultimately jeopardize the very communities we are sworn to protect.

We owe it to every first responder who has put their life on the line to ensure they have the tools they need to come home safely. HB41 is a step in the wrong direction. Let's not let fear dictate policy when lives--both first responders' and civilians'--are at stake.

_Dennis Farris is President of the Austin Retired Police Officers Association and has had a 30-year law enforcement career_." [The Hayride](https://substack.com/redirect/48e87d8f-2784-449d-979c-dd0915121e48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

TOP NEWS "Four Texas school districts at risk for state takeover after 2023 ratings released, " Texas Tribune's Sneha Dey \-- "At least four Texas school districts could be forced to shut down their chronically underperforming schools or submit to a takeover from the state, based on annual state ratings released Thursday morning. The Texas Education Agency released its A-F grades for the 2022-23 school year, the first complete set in five years. Ratings had not been released due to court battles and pauses to the rating system during the COVID-19 pandemic. The Beaumont, Midland, Fort Worth and Wichita Falls school districts all have one or more campuses that failed state ratings for at least four years in a row, putting them at risk of bruising state penalties. Of the 8,539 public schools evaluated in the state, 19.3% got an A. Another 33.6% got a B and 24.7% got a C. About one in five campuses failed to meet academic standards, with 14.8% earning a D and 7.6% earning an F. Performance scores for schools and districts are determined based on three categories: how students perform on state tests and meet college and career readiness benchmarks; how students improve over time; and how well schools are educating their most disadvantaged students. Overall grades declined for many campuses since the 2021-2022 school year. Half of the state's campuses received A or B grades, a decline of about 20 percentage points from the previous school year. The state only released partial scores that year. TEA Commissioner Mike Morath attributed that decline to a drop in academic growth as schools worked to recover from the pandemic. Many school district leaders, meanwhile, have attributed the declines to stricter college and career readiness standards. For the first time, schools had to show that 88% of their graduating high school students were college or career-ready to get an A, up from the 60% benchmark in previous years. About 10,000 more students met the requirements to prove college and career readiness. "We keep raising the bar so that Texas is a leader in preparing students for postsecondary success," Morath said at a press roundtable. The release of the A-F ratings comes after over changes to how schools are scored. More than 120 school districts sought to block the release of the 2023 ratings because they said TEA had not given them adequate notice before rolling out stricter college and career readiness benchmarks. Earlier this month, an appeals court cleared TEA to make the 2023 A-F grades public, ruling that Morath did not overstep his authority when he changed the scoring metrics." FREE SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE ENDED : As of July 11, 2022, we have moved to a paywall for free subscribers. Free subscribers will only receive the top story in their morning email. Free subscribers will need to become paid subscribers to receive full story summaries. #TXLEGE Dennis Farris guest column : "Lives Are on The Line as Texas Lawmakers Debate Drone Ban, " via The Hayride** \-- "I've lost too many friends in the line of duty. When lives are on the line, we must do everything in our power to ensure first responders have the best possible tools to protect themselves and the public. That's why I must weigh in to oppose Texas lawmakers push to pass House Bill 41 - a well-intentioned but misguided piece of legislation that would force law enforcement and firefighters to abandon one of our most effective tools for saving lives: drones. Drones have revolutionized emergency response. They can be deployed instantly, providing officers with real-time intelligence before they step into dangerous situations. In active shooter incidents, fires, search-and-rescue missions, and disaster recovery efforts, drones allow first responders to quickly and accurately assess threats, locate victims, and make high stakes decisions - without putting human lives at unnecessary risk. I've seen it firsthand. When someone is lost in the wilderness or trapped under rubble, thermal imaging on drones has helped locate them when every second counts. When armed suspects flee into the night, drones offer aerial thermal imaging that keeps officers and civilians safe. Drones navigate environments that human responders can't: collapsed buildings, chemical spills, raging floodwaters, and dangerous terrain. Yet, instead of recognizing their life-saving value, HB41 would force police and fire departments to throw out these critical tools because they contain foreign-made parts. Why? There is concern foreign-made drones pose a security threat, but right now there is no specific evidence backing this fear. In fact, Congress already mandated a federal security study on these drones, set to be completed by December 2025. Texas legislators are rushing to ban them before the facts are even in. Legislators shouldn't pass a ban with very real life-and-death consequences based on theoretical threats. Law enforcement has been outspoken against this bill, and their main concern is the rapid timeline the bill imposes for stopping use and procurement of this technology. Departments would have no time to transition their drone programs and no good options for replacing their current drones. Right now, American manufacturers simply do not produce enough drones to replace the foreign-made models at the scale first responders require. Those that are available cost much more and often lack the capabilities law enforcement relies on - meaning agencies will either be forced to cut their drone programs entirely or spend astronomical sums on inferior equipment. It would be like telling people to throw out their iPhone and replace it with a $3,000 flip phone because the chip in their smartphone isn't American-made. This issue shouldn't be about politics or splashy anti-China headlines. Officer safety is on the line. Texas has always stood by its first responders, ensuring we have the support needed to protect our communities. Restricting access to drones will make our work more dangerous, put officers and firefighters at unnecessary risk, and ultimately jeopardize the very communities we are sworn to protect. We owe it to every first responder who has put their life on the line to ensure they have the tools they need to come home safely. HB41 is a step in the wrong direction. Let's not let fear dictate policy when lives--both first responders' and civilians'--are at stake. Dennis Farris is President of the Austin Retired Police Officers Association and has had a 30-year law enforcement career." #TXLEGE "After the failed attempt to impeach AG Paxton, state senators wants to change Texas' impeachment law " ($) "Batteries hold promise of clean, reliable Texas energy, if problems can be overcome " ($) STATE GOVERNMENT " Ag Commissioner Miller Makes Splash at EarthX with Water Warnings" TEXANS IN DC John Cornyn guest column: "I've worked hand-in-glove with President Trump to accomplish his agenda during his first 100 days" ($) 2025 " Business, community leaders rally behind $987M Alamo Colleges bond" BUSINESS NEWS " American Airlines loses $473M as demand falters, momentum 'quickly shifted' on tariffs" ($) " Southwest Airlines posts $149M loss, cuts guidance on 'macroeconomic uncertainty'" ($) NEWS FROM AROUND THE STATE FW REPORT: "Fort Worth Opera returns to Bass Performance Hall with first full-scale production in 6 years " THE TEXAN: "House Partially Passes $3 Billion Dementia Prevention Research Institute of Texas Legislation " AAS: "Gov. * **#TXLEGE**

**Dennis Farris guest column** : "**Lives Are on The Line as Texas Lawmakers Debate Drone Ban,** ” via The Hayride**** \-- "I’ve lost too many friends in the line of duty. When lives are on the line, we must do everything in our power to ensure first responders have the best possible tools to protect themselves and the public. That’s why I must weigh in to oppose Texas lawmakers push to pass House Bill 41 – a well-intentioned but misguided piece of legislation that would force law enforcement and firefighters to abandon one of our most effective tools for saving lives: drones.

Drones have revolutionized emergency response. They can be deployed instantly, providing officers with real-time intelligence before they step into dangerous situations. In active shooter incidents, fires, search-and-rescue missions, and disaster recovery efforts, drones allow first responders to quickly and accurately assess threats, locate victims, and make high stakes decisions – without putting human lives at unnecessary risk.

I’ve seen it firsthand. When someone is lost in the wilderness or trapped under rubble, thermal imaging on drones has helped locate them when every second counts. When armed suspects flee into the night, drones offer aerial thermal imaging that keeps officers and civilians safe. Drones navigate environments that human responders can’t: collapsed buildings, chemical spills, raging floodwaters, and dangerous terrain.

Yet, instead of recognizing their life-saving value, HB41 would force police and fire departments to throw out these critical tools because they contain foreign-made parts. Why? There is concern foreign-made drones pose a security threat, but right now there is no specific evidence backing this fear. In fact, Congress already mandated a federal security study on these drones, set to be completed by December 2025. Texas legislators are rushing to ban them before the facts are even in. Legislators shouldn’t pass a ban with very real life-and-death consequences based on theoretical threats.

Law enforcement has been outspoken against this bill, and their main concern is the rapid timeline the bill imposes for stopping use and procurement of this technology. Departments would have no time to transition their drone programs and no good options for replacing their current drones. Right now, American manufacturers simply do not produce enough drones to replace the foreign-made models at the scale first responders require. Those that are available cost much more and often lack the capabilities law enforcement relies on – meaning agencies will either be forced to cut their drone programs entirely or spend astronomical sums on inferior equipment. It would be like telling people to throw out their iPhone and replace it with a $3,000 flip phone because the chip in their smartphone isn’t American-made.

This issue shouldn’t be about politics or splashy anti-China headlines. Officer safety is on the line. Texas has always stood by its first responders, ensuring we have the support needed to protect our communities. Restricting access to drones will make our work more dangerous, put officers and firefighters at unnecessary risk, and ultimately jeopardize the very communities we are sworn to protect.

We owe it to every first responder who has put their life on the line to ensure they have the tools they need to come home safely. HB41 is a step in the wrong direction. Let’s not let fear dictate policy when lives—both first responders’ and civilians’—are at stake.

_Dennis Farris is President of the Austin Retired Police Officers Association and has had a 30-year law enforcement career_." (limited time) | TOP NEWS "Four Texas school districts at risk for state takeover after 2023 ratings released, ” Texas Tribune's Sneha Dey \-- "At least four Texas school districts could be forced to shut down their chronically underperforming schools or submit to a takeover from the state, based on annual state ratings released Thursday morning. The Texas Education Agency released its A-F grades for the 2022-23 school year, the first complete set in five years. Ratings had not been released due to court battles and pauses to the rating system during the COVID-19 pandemic. The Beaumont, Midland, Fort Worth and Wichita Falls school districts all have one or more campuses that failed state ratings for at least four years in a row, putting them at risk of bruising state penalties. » Of the 8,539 public schools evaluated in the state, 19.3% got an A. Another 33.6% got a B and 24.7% got a C. About one in five campuses failed to meet academic standards, with 14.8% earning a D and 7.6% earning an F. Performance scores for schools and districts are determined based on three categories: how students perform on state tests and meet college and career readiness benchmarks; how students improve over time; and how well schools are educating their most disadvantaged students. » Overall grades declined for many campuses since the 2021-2022 school year. Half of the state’s campuses received A or B grades, a decline of about 20 percentage points from the previous school year. The state only released partial scores that year. TEA Commissioner Mike Morath attributed that decline to a drop in academic growth as schools worked to recover from the pandemic. Many school district leaders, meanwhile, have attributed the declines to stricter college and career readiness standards. For the first time, schools had to show that 88% of their graduating high school students were college or career-ready to get an A, up from the 60% benchmark in previous years. About 10,000 more students met the requirements to prove college and career readiness. “We keep raising the bar so that Texas is a leader in preparing students for postsecondary success,” Morath said at a press roundtable. The release of the A-F ratings comes after over changes to how schools are scored. More than 120 school districts sought to block the release of the 2023 ratings because they said TEA had not given them adequate notice before rolling out stricter college and career readiness benchmarks. Earlier this month, an appeals court cleared TEA to make the 2023 A-F grades public, ruling that Morath did not overstep his authority when he changed the scoring metrics." | FREE SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE ENDED : As of July 11, 2022, we have moved to a paywall for free subscribers. Free subscribers will only receive the top story in their morning email. Free subscribers will need to become paid subscribers to receive full story summaries. | #TXLEGE Dennis Farris guest column : "Lives Are on The Line as Texas Lawmakers Debate Drone Ban, ” via The Hayride \-- "I’ve lost too many friends in the line of duty. When lives are on the line, we must do everything in our power to ensure first responders have the best possible tools to protect themselves and the public. That’s why I must weigh in to oppose Texas lawmakers push to pass House Bill 41 – a well-intentioned but misguided piece of legislation that would force law enforcement and firefighters to abandon one of our most effective tools for saving lives: drones. Drones have revolutionized emergency response. They can be deployed instantly, providing officers with real-time intelligence before they step into dangerous situations. In active shooter incidents, fires, search-and-rescue missions, and disaster recovery efforts, drones allow first responders to quickly and accurately assess threats, locate victims, and make high stakes decisions – without putting human lives at unnecessary risk. I’ve seen it firsthand. When someone is lost in the wilderness or trapped under rubble, thermal imaging on drones has helped locate them when every second counts. When armed suspects flee into the night, drones offer aerial thermal imaging that keeps officers and civilians safe. Drones navigate environments that human responders can’t: collapsed buildings, chemical spills, raging floodwaters, and dangerous terrain. Yet, instead of recognizing their life-saving value, HB41 would force police and fire departments to throw out these critical tools because they contain foreign-made parts. Why? There is concern foreign-made drones pose a security threat, but right now there is no specific evidence backing this fear. In fact, Congress already mandated a federal security study on these drones, set to be completed by December 2025. Texas legislators are rushing to ban them before the facts are even in. Legislators shouldn’t pass a ban with very real life-and-death consequences based on theoretical threats. Law enforcement has been outspoken against this bill, and their main concern is the rapid timeline the bill imposes for stopping use and procurement of this technology. Departments would have no time to transition their drone programs and no good options for replacing their current drones. Right now, American manufacturers simply do not produce enough drones to replace the foreign-made models at the scale first responders require. Those that are available cost much more and often lack the capabilities law enforcement relies on – meaning agencies will either be forced to cut their drone programs entirely or spend astronomical sums on inferior equipment. It would be like telling people to throw out their iPhone and replace it with a $3,000 flip phone because the chip in their smartphone isn’t American-made. This issue shouldn’t be about politics or splashy anti-China headlines. Officer safety is on the line. Texas has always stood by its first responders, ensuring we have the support needed to protect our communities. Restricting access to drones will make our work more dangerous, put officers and firefighters at unnecessary risk, and ultimately jeopardize the very communities we are sworn to protect. We owe it to every first responder who has put their life on the line to ensure they have the tools they need to come home safely. HB41 is a step in the wrong direction. Let’s not let fear dictate policy when lives—both first responders’ and civilians’—are at stake. | | | The savage attack on October 7th and the ongoing war have left countless families in Israel devastated. Entire communities have been displaced. Lives have been shattered. **Homes have been destroyed.**
---
[](http://trk.thedcbugle.com/?xtl=nj7fp644nxypo4dcnjr1nd8kbicc5bpom80a2zrka6s1em7v3fd16qwyig9r22pn1q528rmrlflfxv34z7suefhuebp0sf87lm5mkuv6o3hop6rc4goro6xt&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=sv8mud&__onlt=h)

From the brutality of the attacks in the south to the terror of missiles and bloodshed in the north, they have faced horrors that no one should ever experience. Many fled with only the clothes on their backs, and some have no home to return to. At the **International Christian Embassy Jerusalem (ICEJ),** we refuse to let these precious families suffer alone. God has called us to stand in the gap, bringing hope and aid to those who need it most.
We are providing:

We are hosting a statewide call on Zoom to talk about how we can protect our communities and how to respond to this moment. body:
If Trump gets his way, working families will pay the price! These tariffs will drain the bank accounts of working families, hurt small businesses, and devastate local economies while driving up inflation.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106443476/541541649/800699251?refcode=BLU_EM_LGC_2025-04-24_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NzIwMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ZTVkNmJiYS00NjIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=H4a9kyOr5iwkvEqpWdjLNNdNhjNrfV58x1UOrf_wZHs=)

| Peter,

America’s families are already being stretched thin from sky-high prices at the grocery store to rising prices at the gas station.

Now, Donald Trump is making things worse with a reckless trade war that will raise prices even higher, making it more difficult for hardworking people to support their families.

**There are no winners in a trade war.** Trump’s broad tariffs are nothing more than a tax hike on hardworking Americans.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106443479/541541659/1012657848?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NzIwMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ZTVkNmJiYS00NjIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=H4a9kyOr5iwkvEqpWdjLNNdNhjNrfV58x1UOrf_wZHs=&emci=10a532a3-5320-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=9e5d6bba-4621-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=7377580)
I came to Congress to work with anyone who’s serious about making life more affordable for working families just trying to get by. That’s why I’m proud to support the bipartisan **Trade Review Act** , which would require Congressional oversight and approval over any new tariffs.

If Trump gets his way, _working families will pay the price!_ These tariffs will drain the bank accounts of working families, hurt small businesses, and devastate local economies while driving up inflation.

| Welcome to Keeping Up with Kathryn Harvey. A weekly digest covering South Carolina politics and opportunities for engagement and action in the Upstate.
---
|
# This is what representation looks like.
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| Thank you to Congressman Clyburn for showing up on Tuesday night in Spartanburg for “The People’s Town Hall.” While our South Carolina Republican Delegation (looking at you William Timmons) dodges in-person town halls, Congressman Jim Clyburn is doing what real leaders do: meeting voters face-to-face across the state, including in Republican strongholds. At a time when democracy is under threat, Congressman Clyburn is sounding the alarm and urging South Carolinians to break the silence and stay engaged.When someone asked “What can we do to fight this?” Clyburn replied, **"I am using what is the best of me to fight this - and I want you to use the best of you to fight this.”** Thank you Congressman Clyburn. It was an honor.
---
| [Click here to watch the Town Hall! ](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=2f2a5d1a2a&e=edbde6c9b1)
---
| Meanwhile, when questioned by Upstate news outlets, **Congressman William Timmons** called the town hall on Tuesday **“performative,”** but continues to hide from the people he represents under the guise of **“focusing on Trump’s America First policy”** The constituents of SC-04 have questions, and they deserve answers. It has been over 1,300 days since Congressman William Timmons has hosted a town hall. It begs the question: where exactly is he?

I dive deeper into what is happening at our Statehouse in a conversation with Rep Wendell Jones from Greenville. Make sure to Tune in **Every Wednesday** as I join the crew from [Frogmore Stew - SC’s pop-politics podcast](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=5df02f5aaf&e=edbde6c9b1) \- as their weekly contributor from the Upstate.

| | | | | | | | | | | **190,000+ SC Voters: Check Your Mail!** In an ongoing effort to maintain the integrity of South Carolina’s statewide voter registration list, [**State Election Commission is sending voter confirmation postcards**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=d3e44b5919&e=edbde6c9b1) to 190,000+ who haven't voted since 2020 General Election and not updated their voter info. That you? When it arrives: sign it, date it, and drop it back in the mail within 90 days _(will already be stamped & addressed)_
_**REMINDER:**_**Get your Real ID or start carrying your passport** Starting May 7th, 2025, U.S. air travelers (including those flying domestically) **who** do not present a real ID-compliant license or acceptable alternative like a passport will face additional screening, delays, and may not be permitted past security checkpoint.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | Just three more weeks until the end of legislative session, which boils down to NINE state house working days left to pass any new laws. Bills that don't make it out by May 8th will have to go on the back burner until January 2026. So far, **926** bills introduced, and **9** bills signed into law _(this time in last year's session 31 bills had been signed into law)._
| **State Senators voted to remove Curtis Loftis** South Carolina senators voted 33-8 Monday night to approve a resolution to remove the state treasurer from office after an eight-hour hearing. The resolution needed 31 votes to pass the resolution to oust Curtis Loftis from his position. But he’s not out of a job just yet. The South Carolina House would then have to take up the house where two-thirds of that body would also need to approve a resolution for Loftis to be removed.
**Oppose Senate Bill 32 -**[**Contact your Senator**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=f21c647f2a&e=edbde6c9b1)
---
[ Senate Bill 32](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=bbac07f536&e=edbde6c9b1), which would provide taxpayer-funded incentives to crisis pregnancy centers, has passed its third reading in the Senate and is now headed to the House.
These centers often present themselves as medical facilities but frequently provide misleading or incomplete information about reproductive health.

**Improving care in South Carolina with Senate Bill 2** Last week, while the House was on furlough, the Senate gave final approval to [**Senate Bill 2**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=7559e3538e&e=edbde6c9b1) , a significant step toward improving how South Carolina delivers services for people with disabilities, mental health needs, and substance use disorders. The bill creates a new Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Disabilities by consolidating three existing agencies, aiming to streamline services and improve access.

name: Kristen McDonald Rivet
subject: We just got the news we’ve been fighting for.
body:
|
#
Friend, We just got the news we’ve been fighting for: **After the Trump administration threatened to close it, we secured a commitment that our Social Security office in Saginaw is staying OPEN.** [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106444689/541545424/1780544272?refcode=em-4.24.25-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjAyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NTM2NGFjZC00ODIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=9iBx2LYjyJ-dc8DR_LEwOVibgHw5bQm0awkmREVmLPs=&emci=6285ffab-0221-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=95364acd-4821-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=27257697) **Saginaw Social Security field office to stay open** When the Elon Musk-led GSA quietly added our office to a federal list of properties targeted for closure, we didn’t stay quiet. We demanded answers. Our community rallied. And we refused to let a crucial community resource disappear without a fight. **Now, after months of confusion, silence from the Administration, and sustained public pressure, they have caved and agreed to keep it open.** It shouldn’t take months of consternation for our constituents, two formal letters, a flood of phone calls, and multiple rallies just to get the government to listen. But that’s what it took – and because we refused to back down, we won. This is a big victory for mid-Michigan. And it’s more than just a local win – it’s a playbook for how to fight and win: We organize. We show up. We never let up. But this isn’t the end of the story. The administration still hasn’t explained why these closure lists keep surfacing – and across the country, other offices may be at risk without warning. That’s why I’m asking you to take the next step: **[Will you sign your name to stand against ALL cuts to the Social Security Administration? clean_body: | Friend, We just got the news we’ve been fighting for: After the Trump administration threatened to close it, we secured a commitment that our Social Security office in Saginaw is staying OPEN. Saginaw Social Security field office to stay open When the Elon Musk-led GSA quietly added our office to a federal list of properties targeted for closure, we didn’t stay quiet. We demanded answers. Our community rallied. And we refused to let a crucial community resource disappear without a fight. Now, after months of confusion, silence from the Administration, and sustained public pressure, they have caved and agreed to keep it open. It shouldn’t take months of consternation for our constituents, two formal letters, a flood of phone calls, and multiple rallies just to get the government to listen. But that’s what it took – and because we refused to back down, we won. This is a big victory for mid-Michigan. And it’s more than just a local win – it’s a playbook for how to fight and win: We organize. We show up. We never let up. But this isn’t the end of the story. subject: I’m calling on Hegseth to resign.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Mazie Hirono For Hawaii**
body:
|
#
---
Peter, **Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth leaked military intel for a second time — _and it has to be the last._** I’m calling on Hegseth to resign before his continued missteps result in dangerous conditions for our servicemembers. It’s never been more clear that Hegseth’s loyalty to Donald Trump — not his experience or competence — is what landed him this role. Hegseth has shown a dangerous disregard for procedures that keep military information classified — not once, but twice — and those are the two times we _know_ about! That is in addition to the complete disregard of who exactly was in those Signal chats, such as a reporter for the Atlantic! By using his personal cell phone to communicate sensitive military plans, Hegseth has exposed classified information to potential hackers. I questioned Hegseth at the Senate Armed Services Committee after he was nominated to Trump’s cabinet. I urged against his nomination then because I found him to be unqualified, and in a matter of months he’s proven to be a _**major threat**_ to the safety of our country. **[This is why I’m calling on Defense Secretary Hegseth to resign immediately. I know that looking around here, it can feel impossible for Republicans out here to be defeated.

body:
Our race is already a toss up, and I need your early support to win

| It’s Hillary here. I wanted to make sure you heard that my colleague and friend Haley Stevens is running for the U.S. Senate, and I’m proud to endorse her. Her message is below:
* * *
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106445644/541548334/-873513011?refcode=BLU_EM_HSC_2025-04-24_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4NDgxODA5OS00YjIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=u5FAfvhoxAts2VgtO4QSHWSzOzFsU9GxQMr-d5E6RAQ=)

Hi – this is Congresswoman Haley Stevens writing to you with exciting news: I’m launching my campaign for Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat.

Winning in Michigan is essential to regaining our Democratic Senate majority, and right now The Cook Political Report is rating our race as a “Toss Up.” That means we’re already one of the GOP’s top targets for defeat. Just last year, they spent nearly $80 million trying to buy Michigan’s Senate seat and came up only 0.3% short, so I need your early support to win.

**I want to tell you a bit more about myself and why I’m running.[_But if that’s all you needed to hear and you’re ready to get to work, please chip in whatever you can – split between my campaign and Hillary Scholten – to help hit our $1 million launch goal and become a Founding Donor of my campaign to keep Michigan blue._](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106445645/541548335/-873513011?refcode=BLU_EM_HSC_2025-04-24_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4NDgxODA5OS00YjIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=u5FAfvhoxAts2VgtO4QSHWSzOzFsU9GxQMr-d5E6RAQ=)**
| [CHIP IN → ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106445646/541548336/-873513011?refcode=BLU_EM_HSC_2025-04-24_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4NDgxODA5OS00YjIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=u5FAfvhoxAts2VgtO4QSHWSzOzFsU9GxQMr-d5E6RAQ=)
---
I’m proud to be a lifelong Michigander. I learned the value of hard work by watching my parents – who owned their own landscaping business – build things. Heavy machinery equipment, bobcats, plows, dirt, grease, and grime – it was all part of my childhood.

Later in life, I got the call to give back to the state I love during a time of great uncertainty: the Great Recession. **I can’t tell you how unfathomable it was to hear the words “bankruptcy” and “General Motors” in the same sentence.** So I stepped up to do my part and served as chief of staff for the Auto Rescue initiative under President Obama.

We brought workers, corporations, and union leadership around the same table to stabilize the auto industry. On Friday nights, I’d stay in the office until the late evening and return every call from every Michigander who called our office worried about the future. _In the end, we saved 200,000 Michigan jobs._

I can’t help but see parallels between then and now as we find ourselves in another moment of great uncertainty, thanks to the chaos forced on us by Donald Trump and his billionaire buddy Elon Musk.

People are rightly concerned about rising costs, shoot-from-the-hip tariffs, and attacks on our personal freedoms. **Michiganders need a fighter in their corner – and that’s who I’ve been my entire life.**

Sign our petition to stop ACTIVE voter suppression by Congress.
[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106448339/541557342/664783965?ms=042425_saveact&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNV08vMS83NjczNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNjE2NjkyOC01MzIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QIJ9ErwsLtchtYiPCDCeZeAPtdqO7GZTcJ-Zy_IkIj0=&emci=b0133565-4121-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=a6166928-5321-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=864787)
Peter, **our voting rights are under attack.**
The SAVE Act is a bill under review in the Senate that could disenfranchise millions of American voters, especially people who changed their last name upon marriage. It would require all voters to provide **in-person proof of U.S. citizenship,** like a passport or birth certificate, when registering to vote or updating their voter registration.
**This is voter disenfranchisement and an attempt to silence our voices, plain and simple. **
We need to pressure the Senate to stop this cruel voter suppression bill. **[**_Please sign this petition with our partners at Common Cause to demand the Senate vote NO:_**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106448340/541557343/388988323?source=041625swap-cia&referrer=group-care-in-action-2025&ms=042425_saveact&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNV08vMS83NjczNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNjE2NjkyOC01MzIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QIJ9ErwsLtchtYiPCDCeZeAPtdqO7GZTcJ-Zy_IkIj0=&emci=b0133565-4121-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=a6166928-5321-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=864787)**
**_**********__[Sign our petition](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106448341/541557344/388988323?source=041625swap-cia&referrer=group-care-in-action-2025&ms=042425_saveact&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNV08vMS83NjczNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNjE2NjkyOC01MzIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QIJ9ErwsLtchtYiPCDCeZeAPtdqO7GZTcJ-Zy_IkIj0=&emci=b0133565-4121-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=a6166928-5321-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=864787)__**********_**
Over 21 million Americans who are eligible to vote don’t have easy access to the documents this law would require for voter registration, making it even more difficult for people to vote.
The SAVE Act would effectively block access to the ballot for so many care workers and caregivers in our community — who work long, irregular hours and often need to register to vote online or by mail. The requirement to show proof of citizenship in-person would _effectively end online and mail voter registration nationwide — which was crucial in expanding access to the ballot box for eligible voters._
It would also purge voters from voting rolls without notice, and cause long lines and voting delays at voter registration offices.
As our endorsed Care Champion Rep. Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) put it, “It is a slap in the face for all of the women generally and Black women specifically who gave blood, sweat and tears for the right to vote.”
The Senate needs to stand up for voting rights. ****_**[**_Can you sign this petition with our partners at Common Cause to tell the Senate to reject the SAVE Act?_**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/106448342/541557345/388988323?source=041625swap-cia&referrer=group-care-in-action-2025&ms=042425_saveact&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNV08vMS83NjczNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNjE2NjkyOC01MzIxLWYwMTEtOGIzZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QIJ9ErwsLtchtYiPCDCeZeAPtdqO7GZTcJ-Zy_IkIj0=&emci=b0133565-4121-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&emdi=a6166928-5321-f011-8b3d-0022482a9fb7&ceid=864787)**_****

President Donald Trump met with wounded veterans in the White House today and he **[couldn't help but laugh](https://substack.com/redirect/cf028ed7-8b88-4654-9530-be6b3f49e358?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** when something unexpected occurred.
Trump noticed one of the soldiers had brought a picture of Joe Biden with him.
"Who's in that picture?" Trump asked the soldier. **[Watch what happens next:](https://substack.com/redirect/cf028ed7-8b88-4654-9530-be6b3f49e358?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/cf028ed7-8b88-4654-9530-be6b3f49e358?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/cf028ed7-8b88-4654-9530-be6b3f49e358?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"Oh, it's a picture of Joe Biden and it says 'Let's Go Brandon' on it," he replied.
Trump and the whole room immediately burst into laughter, "Oh! I'm saying 'what was that picture?' That's great," Trump joked.
After meeting with the wounded American heroes and taking some questions from the press, the President gave the veterans some Presidential Challenge Coins made of gun metal to thank them for their service to our country.
**["I think you're gonna really like them,](https://substack.com/redirect/cf028ed7-8b88-4654-9530-be6b3f49e358?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** these are the best!" Trump told the soldiers, handing them out to each of them.

Peter,

You may have seen the reports: Donald Trump just took action against ActBlue, the online donation platform used across the Democratic ecosystem and by countless campaigns and organizations.

Let's be clear: when Trump and his allies lash out, it's not because they're winning. It's because they're afraid.

Afraid of the momentum Democrats are building. Afraid of the women we're helping to elect. Afraid of you — and the grassroots power that's fueling this fight.

As EMILYs List President Jessica Mackler put it:
_"Republicans are poised to lose big in the midterms, so Trump is doing what he does best: distract, create chaos, increase anxiety, and instill fear. But Trump's focus on ActBlue tells us one thing: they fear Democratic power and the countless grassroots donors across the country who are fueling the resistance. By completing this survey and returning it to me as soon as possible, you will help Hillsdale College more clearly understand the views of mainstream Americans concerning this issue—views we will make available to policymakers and opinion leaders.

You can complete the National Survey on Presidential Selection by using the link below:

For most of our nation's history, the Electoral College, as devised by the Framers of our Constitution, was not controversial. Indeed, it was considered essential to preserving free and representative government.

But today, more than a dozen states have joined together in an attempt to undermine this constitutional bulwark of liberty.

This movement to undermine the Constitution has grown largely because of the failure of America's schools to provide young people with a proper grounding in American civics—too many Americans simply don't understand the importance of the Constitution, including the Electoral College, to liberty.

Because of this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, directly teaching millions of Americans in all 50 states.

These efforts, which aim to counter the Left's domination over most of our schools, include:

Teaching millions of citizens nationwide through free online courses, such as "Constitution 101" and "The Great American Story: A Land of Hope;"

Reaching over six million households and businesses nationwide with Imprimis, Hillsdale's free digest of liberty;

Promoting constitutional education through social media outlets popular with young people;

Sending millions of pocket-size copies of America's founding documents to citizens and K-12 schools across America; and

Restoring excellence to K-12 education by helping establish and guiding classical K-12 schools nationwide and providing, free of charge, Hillsdale's American classical K-12 curriculum (including American civics) to thousands of American educators and homeschoolers.

Your answers to the National Survey on Presidential Selection will help Hillsdale form the most effective strategy to educate millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to liberty—including the importance of the Electoral College.

And this is especially important in this critical time for America's future.

So please share your views on this urgent topic by completing our National Survey on Presidential Selection and returning it to me as soon as possible. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

College Football’s 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. Is there such a thing as a MAGA Lefty? Well Batya Ungar-Sargon is going to fill us in on today's show, she is joined by Steve Cortes and Jenn Pellegrino for an all star Thursday panel. As President Trump reshaped the Republican party with America First policies, the GOP became the party of the working people. President Trump has attracted people like Batya with American worker protectionist, anti-war, and fair trade practice policies. It's a stark contrast to the Bush era Republican party but has not led to a complete party switch as we saw with the Supreme Court election in Wisconsin. So while President Trump has made significant strides, being MAGA does not necessarily mean you are a Republican. Linda McMahon announced that the department of education will start collections on student loans, taking the $1.7 Trillion debt off the taxpayer's back. The Ivy League gets more public money than any other state or public university. Meaning that Americans are investing in universities that are creating little woke radicals and President Trump is taking a stand against the anti-American agenda most of these schools espouse. MAGA media is on the rise as hypocrites like Jake Tapper are now trying to profit off the lie they perpetrated about Biden's mental acuity. President Trump will attend Pope Francis' funeral even with the Pope's previous disagreement with the president on immigration. Like every Thursday, stick around for the winners and losers of the week!

America's birth rate is in decline--and MAGA Republicans think they've found the solution. Donald Trump is apparently proposing a $5,000 check for parents who have a baby. On its face, this is not just performative--it's offensively stupid. It fails to address the economic crises afflicting tens of millions of families, and offers an impotent idea (pun intended) that will do nothing but increase poverty and suffering. Meanwhile, it ignores the actual and proven solutions to ensuring healthier American families. **Let 's Address This.**

## Why $5K Is A Farce
First, let me remind the reader that the Trump regime is actively engaging in [Structural Eugenics](https://substack.com/redirect/d7a974e0-ceb7-4159-9424-bfe4e0d78eff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which is particularly targeting Black and brown communities, as well as low income communities. The MAGA movement has long feared the demographic change in America in which white Americans are expected to become a minority by 2045. There's an argument--a very good argument--that Trump's attempts to increase the birth rate with a $5K bribe is part of the fear right wing white conservatives have of becoming a racial minority again in America.
To which I ask--why, are minorities mistreated or something in America?
But we'll revisit that argument at another time. For now, let's look at the math of having a baby vs $5000, and I think you'll see that the math isn't mathing.
The average cost to have a baby in America is somewhere between $20,000 and $30,000, and up to $50,000 if you don't have health insurance (which 20 million women don't have). The average annual cost of childcare is $20,000. And the median home price is $419,000. Donald Trump thinks a one time $5000 check should be enough to cover all of the above. Meanwhile, MAGA Republicans refuse to enact actual economically just policies to facilitate the stability and growth of healthy families. For example, MAGA Republicans (and some corporate Dems to be sure) refuse to:
* Raise the federal minimum wage (stuck at $7.25/hour since 2009)
* Increase taxes on billionaires or large corporations
* Make the Child Tax Credit permanent
* Fund universal pre-K
* Cancel student debt or pass any kind of tuition reform, period
* Build affordable housing
* Pass universal healthcare
* Protect reproductive freedom (which has been proven to increase life expectancy for children and mothers)

In other words, they want people to give birth in a nation that actively punishes them for doing so--and hope no one notices their band aid solution is a farce.
## The Silent Generation Didn't Need $5K for the Baby Boom--They Enjoyed Good Policy
Trump's $5,000-for-a-baby plan isn't just absurd--it's ahistorical. The U.S. had its most significant baby boom when the top marginal tax rate was between 77% and 91%. That tax structure wasn't a burden. It was a design feature of an economy that invested in working families. And it worked.
For those who argue that no one actually paid those high tax rates, you're inadvertently making the case for why they were so effective. The wealthy structured their accumulated wealth in ways that avoided extreme tax liability. How? By _actually_ doing what the trickle down scam _claims_ to do, meaningfully reinvesting in society:
1. They paid their workers a living wage.
2. They offered real retirement pensions.
3. They provided comprehensive health benefits.
4. They kept CEO salaries in check. In 1965, the CEO-to-worker pay ratio was about 20:1. Today, it's over 350:1.
5. And the higher tax rates allowed the Federal Government to build the national highway system, electrify America into its rural areas, afford the GI Bill, and afford subsidized housing via the FHA. (Granted the latter two were disgraced with Jim Crow legislation that excised Black Americans).

This isn't economic nostalgia--it's economic literacy, it's proven American history. The United States created a thriving middle class through public investment, strong labor laws, and equitable taxation. None of this was accidental.

## MAGA's Baby Bonus Is a Distraction
What Trump and MAGA Republicans are offering isn't a solution--it's a distraction. A $5,000 bonus in an economy where parents are spending $53,000 before a child turns one is a cruel joke, not serious policy. It's a bribe dressed as a band-aid on a system they've broken and continue to further tear down.
And worse, they have no intention of addressing the root causes of the problem--growing wealth and income inequality. Why? Because that would require taxing billionaires, regulating predatory industries, and investing in workers--things MAGA Republicans are ideologically and financially opposed to.
## The Real Solution? Structural Reform
If we actually want to address falling birth rates, we must confront the systemic economic barriers young people face, so that they can make the choice to start a family if and how they wish, without economic pressures devastating their futures. This includes, but is not limited to:
* Universal healthcare so pregnancy isn't a financial death sentence
* Affordable housing so people can raise families without being rent-burdened
* Paid parental leave so parents don't have to choose between bonding with their newborn or losing their job
* Free or low-cost childcare so both parents can work if they choose
* Tuition-free college and student debt cancellation so families aren't crushed before they begin
* Living wages and strong labor rights so workers aren't working three jobs to stay afloat

If we want a baby boom, we need an economic boom for working people. And that requires courageous policy--not shallow gimmicks. All of the above is possible for two reasons. One, because we've done it before, and we know it works. And two, because taxing billionaires and billion dollar corporations doesn't hurt our economy, it expands our economy by growing our middle class and strengthening local communities.
## Final Thought: Stop the Billionaire Bootlicking
Every time someone defends the ultra-wealthy by saying, "But they don't even pay those high tax rates," they miss the point entirely. The point of high marginal tax rates wasn't to force collection with no alternative--it was to incentivize reinvestment in the working class as the preferred alternative. It forced the super wealthy to grow companies by investing in workers, rather than to grow their bank accounts by hoarding ill gotten wealth.
When the top tax rate was high, the super wealthy did not so easily hoard wealth. They spread it--to workers, to communities, to infrastructure--and it worked. It built a society where having a family wasn't an act of economic masochism. It was a basic human right afforded to ordinary working families.
If you want to solve the so-called "baby problem," tax billionaires fairly, invest in people, protect healthcare, make living affordable, and stop coddling corporate greed. Ensure young people have the economic stability and freedom to choose when and how to start a family without the dread of medical bankruptcy, illness, or death hanging over their shoulder should something go wrong. Families cannot survive, much less thrive, with a one-time check that barely covers the cost of pregnancy, let alone birth.
So let's stop pretending otherwise.

Why Trump's apparent plan to give $5000 to new parents is breathtakingly impotent | | | Apr 24 | | | | | | | | | | | | America's birth rate is in decline--and MAGA Republicans think they've found the solution. Donald Trump is apparently proposing a $5,000 check for parents who have a baby. On its face, this is not just performative--it's offensively stupid. It fails to address the economic crises afflicting tens of millions of families, and offers an impotent idea (pun intended) that will do nothing but increase poverty and suffering. Meanwhile, it ignores the actual and proven solutions to ensuring healthier American families. Let 's Address This. I am doing everything in my power to raise awareness on human rights and justice. I cannot do it alone. I hope you consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. | | ---|---|--- Credit: Threelilmonkeyes Why $5K Is A Farce First, let me remind the reader that the Trump regime is actively engaging in , which is particularly targeting Black and brown communities, as well as low income communities. The MAGA movement has long feared the demographic change in America in which white Americans are expected to become a minority by 2045. There's an argument--a very good argument--that Trump's attempts to increase the birth rate with a $5K bribe is part of the fear right wing white conservatives have of becoming a racial minority again in America. To which I ask--why, are minorities mistreated or something in America? But we'll revisit that argument at another time. For now, let's look at the math of having a baby vs $5000, and I think you'll see that the math isn't mathing. The average cost to have a baby in America is somewhere between $20,000 and $30,000, and up to $50,000 if you don't have health insurance (which 20 million women don't have). The average annual cost of childcare is $20,000. And the median home price is $419,000. Donald Trump thinks a one time $5000 check should be enough to cover all of the above. Meanwhile, MAGA Republicans refuse to enact actual economically just policies to facilitate the stability and growth of healthy families. For example, MAGA Republicans (and some corporate Dems to be sure) refuse to: Raise the federal minimum wage (stuck at $7.25/hour since 2009) Increase taxes on billionaires or large corporations Make the Child Tax Credit permanent Fund universal pre-K Cancel student debt or pass any kind of tuition reform, period Build affordable housing Pass universal healthcare Protect reproductive freedom (which has been proven to increase life expectancy for children and mothers) In other words, they want people to give birth in a nation that actively punishes them for doing so--and hope no one notices their band aid solution is a farce. The Silent Generation Didn't Need $5K for the Baby Boom--They Enjoyed Good Policy Trump's $5,000-for-a-baby plan isn't just absurd--it's ahistorical. The U.S. had its most significant baby boom when the top marginal tax rate was between 77% and 91%. That tax structure wasn't a burden. It was a design feature of an economy that invested in working families. And it worked. For those who argue that no one actually paid those high tax rates, you're inadvertently making the case for why they were so effective. The wealthy structured their accumulated wealth in ways that avoided extreme tax liability. How? By actually doing what the trickle down scam claims to do, meaningfully reinvesting in society: 1. They paid their workers a living wage. 2. They offered real retirement pensions. 3. They provided comprehensive health benefits. 4. They kept CEO salaries in check. In 1965, the CEO-to-worker pay ratio was about 20:1. Today, it's over 350:1. 5. And the higher tax rates allowed the Federal Government to build the national highway system, electrify America into its rural areas, afford the GI Bill, and afford subsidized housing via the FHA. (Granted the latter two were disgraced with Jim Crow legislation that excised Black Americans). This isn't economic nostalgia--it's economic literacy, it's proven American history. The United States created a thriving middle class through public investment, strong labor laws, and equitable taxation. None of this was accidental. If you 're finding value in this article, please join our movement and subscribe. MAGA's Baby Bonus Is a Distraction What Trump and MAGA Republicans are offering isn't a solution--it's a distraction. A $5,000 bonus in an economy where parents are spending $53,000 before a child turns one is a cruel joke, not serious policy. It's a bribe dressed as a band-aid on a system they've broken and continue to further tear down. And worse, they have no intention of addressing the root causes of the problem--growing wealth and income inequality. Why? Because that would require taxing billionaires, regulating predatory industries, and investing in workers--things MAGA Republicans are ideologically and financially opposed to. The Real Solution? Structural Reform If we actually want to address falling birth rates, we must confront the systemic economic barriers young people face, so that they can make the choice to start a family if and how they wish, without economic pressures devastating their futures. This includes, but is not limited to: Universal healthcare so pregnancy isn't a financial death sentence Affordable housing so people can raise families without being rent-burdened Paid parental leave so parents don't have to choose between bonding with their newborn or losing their job Free or low-cost childcare so both parents can work if they choose Tuition-free college and student debt cancellation so families aren't crushed before they begin Living wages and strong labor rights so workers aren't working three jobs to stay afloat If we want a baby boom, we need an economic boom for working people. And that requires courageous policy--not shallow gimmicks. All of the above is possible for two reasons. One, because we've done it before, and we know it works. And two, because taxing billionaires and billion dollar corporations doesn't hurt our economy, it expands our economy by growing our middle class and strengthening local communities. Final Thought: Stop the Billionaire Bootlicking Every time someone defends the ultra-wealthy by saying, "But they don't even pay those high tax rates," they miss the point entirely. The point of high marginal tax rates wasn't to force collection with no alternative--it was to incentivize reinvestment in the working class as the preferred alternative. It forced the super wealthy to grow companies by investing in workers, rather than to grow their bank accounts by hoarding ill gotten wealth. When the top tax rate was high, the super wealthy did not so easily hoard wealth. They spread it--to workers, to communities, to infrastructure--and it worked. It built a society where having a family wasn't an act of economic masochism. It was a basic human right afforded to ordinary working families. If you want to solve the so-called "baby problem," tax billionaires fairly, invest in people, protect healthcare, make living affordable, and stop coddling corporate greed. Ensure young people have the economic stability and freedom to choose when and how to start a family without the dread of medical bankruptcy, illness, or death hanging over their shoulder should something go wrong. Families cannot survive, much less thrive, with a one-time check that barely covers the cost of pregnancy, let alone birth. So let's stop pretending otherwise. Peter, I'm reaching out because you may have seen news about Donald Trump’s new attack on ActBlue — a clear attempt to shut down his political opposition and consolidate MAGA power. For years, ActBlue has been the main way millions of Americans give to Democratic candidates and progressive causes they believe in — including our work at the National Democratic Redistricting Committee. **So let me make this very clear: Trump’s action is a blatant abuse of power, and it’s an outrageous, baseless attempt to stifle his critics. ** If you want to know why he’s going after a grassroots fundraising platform, just look at what this movement accomplished in Wisconsin earlier this month. Elon Musk — one of Trump's closest allies and the wealthiest man on earth — spent millions to try to influence the outcome of that state supreme court race. But the far right _lost_. Why? Because grassroots Democrats organized — and a whole bunch of people donated to make sure that an election like that couldn't be bought. This grassroots victory wouldn't have been possible without a platform like ActBlue. Small-dollar donations are fundamental to a healthy democracy. When millions of us pool our resources to support candidates we believe in, our elections can reflect the will of the people rather than the interests of the wealthy few. And Trump’s attack on ActBlue fits into the broader right-wing agenda of silencing voters, punishing opponents, and seizing power at any cost — through laws that make it harder to vote, maps that make it impossible for communities to elect candidates of their choosing, and outright attempts to steal elections (like what’s happening in North Carolina’s state supreme court race). **ActBlue is still up and running because they refuse to back down — and as they fight back, we’ll continue to defend the right of the American people to participate in our democracy.** I’m so grateful to have you in this fight alongside us. Sincerely, Marina Marina Jenkins

clean_body: This is a blatant abuse of power and an attempt to shut down political opposition. | Peter, I'm reaching out because you may have seen news about Donald Trump’s new attack on ActBlue — a clear attempt to shut down his political opposition and consolidate MAGA power. For years, ActBlue has been the main way millions of Americans give to Democratic candidates and progressive causes they believe in — including our work at the National Democratic Redistricting Committee. So let me make this very clear: Trump’s action is a blatant abuse of power, and it’s an outrageous, baseless attempt to stifle his critics. If you want to know why he’s going after a grassroots fundraising platform, just look at what this movement accomplished in Wisconsin earlier this month. Elon Musk — one of Trump's closest allies and the wealthiest man on earth — spent millions to try to influence the outcome of that state supreme court race. But the far right lost. Why? Because grassroots Democrats organized — and a whole bunch of people donated to make sure that an election like that couldn't be bought. This grassroots victory wouldn't have been possible without a platform like ActBlue. Small-dollar donations are fundamental to a healthy democracy. When millions of us pool our resources to support candidates we believe in, our elections can reflect the will of the people rather than the interests of the wealthy few. And Trump’s attack on ActBlue fits into the broader right-wing agenda of silencing voters, punishing opponents, and seizing power at any cost — through laws that make it harder to vote, maps that make it impossible for communities to elect candidates of their choosing, and outright attempts to steal elections (like what’s happening in North Carolina’s state supreme court race). ActBlue is still up and running because they refuse to back down — and as they fight back, we’ll continue to defend the right of the American people to participate in our democracy. I’m so grateful to have you in this fight alongside us. clean_body: | | | Peter, Donald Trump has just signed a memo directing his Attorney General to launch a politically-motivated investigation into ActBlue. 1 Virtually every single progressive candidate and campaign uses the platform to raise money. And it’s how most people give to us too. For years, ActBlue has been a key piece of the infrastructure that has empowered regular people, giving a few dollars at a time, to fuel progressive campaigns and organizations — and to take on the billionaire class and corporate money that funds the other side. That’s exactly why Trump is going after them now. He wants to make it harder for working people to contribute to campaigns and groups, and easier for billionaires like Elon Musk to buy elections for Republicans with their multimillion-dollar checks. This move is straight out of Trump’s go-to fascist playbook. Trump and his billionaire handlers know they can’t out-organize us. They know they are losing the support of the public on issue after issue. The only move they have is to keep trying to bully and threaten everyone who opposes them. That’s exactly why we cannot and will not be paralyzed into inaction. It’s up to us to show Trump, Musk, and MAGA that their attacks will only make our movement grow stronger. body:
The Supreme Court — Donald Trump's Supreme Court -- rules that his administration must facilitate the return of Mr. Garcia to this country.

I am writing to ask you to do something I haven't asked of you in a while. I am writing to ask you to make a donation to a congressional campaign.
California Congressman Robert Garcia just returned from a trip to El Salvador where he - and several other members of Congress -- tried to meet with Kilmar Abrego Garcia.
Here is the truth:
I don't think anyone trusts the Trump administration to run around the country scooping people off the streets and sending them to foreign prisons without some kind of court hearing to prove they are who the administration says they are.
In the particular case of Mr. Abrego Garcia, the Trump administration admitted in a court of law that he was wrongfully detained and deported.
Now Trump is even talking about doing it to American citizens, "the homegrowns" as he calls them. What we are seeing play out now is just the first step.
But it's bigger than even that.
The Supreme Court -- Donald Trump's Supreme Court -- ruled that his administration must facilitate the return of Mr. Abrego Garcia to this country.
Trump has just decided to ignore that order, and other court orders from lower courts. He is just blatantly and objectively defying the courts, the rule of law, and our system of checks and balances.
Congressman Garcia's visit helped to highlight ALL OF THIS and it's one of the reasons Trump's approval rating is sinking like a stone -- even on the issue of immigration.
He deserves our thanks. So if you can:

The power of the people will ALWAYS be greater than the people in power.
# [](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/203?t=1&akid=249%2E181023%2EkshZa2)
Team — In his latest move to demolish democracy through a thousand cuts, President Trump is calling for a sham investigation into ActBlue, the most significant vehicle that Democratic candidates and nonprofit organizations use to raise money from supporters around the country.
**It’s incredible. It’s un-American. And it’s just another step in this administration's playbook to dismantle democracy.**
Trying to shut down ActBlue. Pushing for a federal law to make it harder for married women (and just about everyone else) to vote. Dismantling protections for election workers and our voting systems.
In just THREE months, Trump and his administration have chipped away at our power — and our right — to hold elected leaders accountable through secure, accessible elections.
Oligarchs rise in silence. They find power in our exhaustion, using chaos, confusion, and fear to mute our voices.
**It’s time for all of us to say clearly and unequivocally that these efforts to destroy the foundation of our country and eliminate our voice will not succeed on our watch.**
We should use this moment to build our party, our power, and our plans to win in 2026 — and beyond.
**[And I know we will win. Because the power of the people will ALWAYS be greater than the people in power. Add your name to join me in the fight.](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/signup/2504-democracy-petition?refcode=AU_JMB_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20250424_PM1_V1_S1&email=&akid=249%2E181023%2EkshZa2)**

We’ve got work to do. So let’s go.
— Jocelyn

Peter,

Palestinian activist and Columbia University graduate Mahmoud Khalil
missed the birth of his child this week as he remains stuck in an ICE
detention center just for participating in peaceful protests.

The Trump administration denied Mahmoud’s request for temporary release to
